speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you are experiencing fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for acute sinusitis; can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and what specific antibiotic you were prescribed?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: It sounds like your symptoms persisted after your sinusitis improved; can you describe the characteristics of your flank pain, such as whether it radiates to your groin or is accompanied by chills?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Blood Cultures.

I need to check your urine for infection and culture your blood to see if there is a bacteremia, especially since you developed a rash on amoxicillin and symptoms worsened after switching to cephalexin. Please also tell me if you have noticed any blood in your urine or increased urinary frequency.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis (AIN)

The presence of binucleated eosinophilic cells (eosinophiluria) in the urine, combined with your history of developing a rash after taking amoxicillin and experiencing persistent flank pain and fever, strongly suggests an allergic reaction to the antibiotics rather than a bacterial infection like pyelonephritis.
